overview:
Democratic incumbent George Whitesides seeks a second term in a district whose partisan lean favors his party by six points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $4.4 million and holding $2.3 million on hand, while Republican Jason Gibbs has raised about $400,000. Outside groups have spent in support of Whitesides, with little activity on the other side.

No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, money, and market pricing. Prediction markets put Whitesides' chances near 96 percent, slightly below what the raw fundamentals would suggest but firmly in favorite territory. The result is a clear Democratic edge, though with somewhat more uncertainty than a typical Safe rating given the absence of survey data and Whitesides' relatively short tenure in the seat.
